name: Opus 5 dispersion
strategy: Beta-matched dispersion repositioned for a stagflationary, two-sided-policy regime: a 55% long basket of ten large caps screened for high residual-to-SPY volatility and low pairwise residual correlation, concentrated into the two legs whose idiosyncratic drivers are confirmed by hard data (CME record rate-futures volumes, NEM record gold/FCF), with the impaired low-income-consumer and catastrophe-exposed legs cut or trimmed, hedged by a 36.5% SPY short sized to the basket's 0.66 estimated beta for net index beta of roughly zero, 8.5% cash.
reassessment_note: Three things changed in the 48 hours since this leg filled, and each hits a named premise of the book of record. (1) The regime label is stale. My strategy of record was built for a 'Fed-hiking' regime; the 10-02 payrolls print (29k jobs, unemployment up to 4.2%) cut October hike odds from 64% to 16% and the policy path is now genuinely two-sided -- weak labor against 3.7% headline PCE, with the Fed itself not forecasting 2% until 2029. That is stagflation, not tightening, and it re-ranks my legs rather than invalidating the structure. (2) Two legs are fundamentally impaired, both on the low-income consumer, which the weak jobs print makes worse rather than better. LVS is printing fresh 52-week lows on Macau hold and VIP softness with a Hold consensus -- I am cutting it to zero rather than holding a long whose residual is moving against me for fundamental reasons. DG's trade-down thesis is broken by DG's own management, which flagged 'spending exhaustion' and rural customers limiting trips on elevated fuel; the stock is -22.6% over three months and its next print is not until December, so it carries impairment with no catalyst inside my window. Trimmed 5.0 to 3.0 rather than zero because it is already heavily de-rated at ~16x. (3) TRV carries a dated adverse catalyst I did not own when I sized it. A late-September Northeast nor'easter hit Travelers harder than any other listed P&C carrier given its mid-Atlantic and Northeast commercial and personal lines concentration, and Q3 lands 10-16 -- inside this holding period. The stock is up since my fill, so it is not priced. Cutting 6.0 to 2.5 and tightening the stop to 12%. Against those cuts I am concentrating into the two residuals that hard data confirms rather than reaching for new names: CME 7 to 9 on record September ADV of 31.8m contracts (+22% y/y), record Q3 ADV, rate ADV +22% and Treasury futures +42% -- the one thing the jobs shock unambiguously raised is policy volatility, and CME monetizes it with the quarter's volumes already banked ahead of its ~10-21 print and the 10-27/28 FOMC; and NEM 4.5 to 8 on gold above $4,500, record quarterly FCF, and dovish repricing into 3.7% inflation pushing real rates down, which is the cleanest macro-confirmed residual I own. These two are low-beta and uncorrelated with each other (exchange volumes vs bullion), so the concentration does not cost me dispersion breadth. I examined CF Industries as an orthogonal inflation-levered add and rejected it: +55% YTD with neutral analysts and a specific late-2026 China urea-flood risk fails my own screen. I kept SPY as the hedge instrument rather than switching to equal-weight RSP, which I considered seriously: with top-10 concentration at a 50-year extreme and the Cboe implied-correlation index resuming its decline, shorting the cap-weighted index against a non-mega-cap basket is an intended part of this book's edge, not an accidental factor bet. I am staying fully inside the dispersion mandate and not drifting directional -- net index beta is ~-0.2% of NAV. Structurally this is a deliberately good moment to be long single-stock dispersion against short index: constituent implied vol has compressed since late July while implied correlation falls into the October earnings cycle (Q3 season opens 10-08, banks 10-13/14, consensus +29% EPS growth), the seasonal window when the constituent-minus-index vol spread widens. Total turnover is ~20% of NAV, which at 2bps equity frictions costs a few cents -- this is a surgical repositioning, not the full churn the book of record would have cost. Eleven weeks at +0.63% with roughly zero beta-adjusted alpha is the honest reason I am not simply holding: the structure is right, the leg-level composition was not.

positions.thesis: Largest weight because it is the only leg whose driver was strengthened rather than weakened by the 10-02 jobs shock. CME reported record September average daily volume of 31.8m contracts, +22% y/y, record Q3 ADV of 29.4m, interest-rate ADV +22% and Treasury futures/options ADV +42%, plus all-time open-interest highs in Ultra 10-Year and Ultra Bond and a new FX OI record. The quarter's volumes are already banked ahead of the ~10-21 print, so the earnings catalyst is de-risked to the upside, and a two-sided policy path into the 10-27/28 FOMC with the 10-year at 5.28% keeps hedging demand elevated through my window. Its residual is driven by contract volume and open interest, which is orthogonal to every other leg here, and its ~0.55 beta lets me carry a 9% weight without inflating the SPY short. Sized up from 7.0; 13% stop is tight because low residual vol means a 13% move is a genuine thesis break, not noise.

The cleanest macro-confirmed residual in the book and the direct beneficiary of exactly what changed this week. Gold above $4,500/oz on central-bank accumulation and inflation hedging, with Newmont realizing $4,414/oz in Q2 against ~$1,680 AISC, generating record free cash flow ($2.2bn in Q2, $3.1bn in Q1) while holding its ~5.3m oz 2026 production guide. Dovish repricing of the October hike into 3.7% headline PCE pushes real rates down, which is the single most reliable input to the gold price, and 17 Strong Buy ratings with a ~$141 mean target sit ~17% above the mark. Sized up from 4.5 to 8.0. Gold-miner residuals are nearly uncorrelated with the financial, healthcare and industrial legs here, which is why this is the right place to concentrate rather than adding a second miner that would just duplicate the bullion factor. Wide 20% stop respects miner residual volatility; TP raised to 40% from 35% because truncating upside in a record-price regime is the wrong error.

Best-performing leg of the current fill at +5.68% and the purest residual in the basket: drug-distribution economics are fee-for-service on script volume, so earnings are close to insensitive to both the labor market and the rate path that just repriced. In a stagflationary tape where I am cutting discretionary-consumer exposure, non-deferrable pharmaceutical volume is the right kind of defensiveness, and unlike a staples retailer it has no low-income-spending dependency. Low ~0.55 beta so it adds residual exposure cheaply in hedge terms, and its idiosyncratic drivers (generics pricing, specialty mix, opioid-litigation runoff) are uncorrelated with CI's medical-cost-trend residual despite the shared sector label. Added 0.5 on continued relative strength.

Managed care residual driven by medical cost trend and pharmacy-benefit economics, which is genuinely orthogonal to rates, oil and the consumer -- the three macro axes that moved this week. Essentially flat since the 09-30 fill (-0.48%), so there is no momentum or valuation reason to disturb it, and a payer's earnings power is set by repricing cycles rather than by payrolls. Held and nudged up 0.5 as part of redeploying the LVS and TRV proceeds into legs whose theses survived this week's data intact rather than into new names researched in an afternoon.

Second-best leg of the current fill at +2.30% and held at unchanged weight. The farm-machinery replacement cycle and dealer inventory destocking are a residual driver shared with nothing else in this basket, and CME's record September soybean open interest of 1.12m contracts is independent corroboration that ag activity and grain hedging are running hot rather than cooling. At ~0.95 beta this is one of only two legs carrying meaningful index sensitivity, which is why I am not sizing it up despite the positive residual -- doing so would force a larger SPY short and raise gross without adding diversification.

Held unchanged at +2.42% since the fill. Edge delivery and security revenue is contracted and subscription-like, so the residual is driven by the security-vs-delivery mix shift rather than by the rate path, and crucially it is the one technology-sector residual I own at a size that does not meaningfully offset the deliberate short-mega-cap-concentration exposure embedded in the SPY hedge. Akamai is also not an AI-capex story, which is what keeps its residual correlation to the Nasdaq complex low enough to be useful here rather than duplicative of the index leg. 18% stop reflects higher residual volatility than the financial and healthcare legs.

Naval shipbuilding backlog is multi-year, congressionally appropriated and almost entirely insensitive to both the consumer and the policy rate, which is the profile I want more of after cutting LVS and trimming DG. In a stagflationary regime where I am reducing cyclical-demand exposure, contracted defense revenue with inflation-adjustment mechanics on long-cycle programs is a defensive residual that does not pay for its defensiveness with a bond-proxy duration exposure the way a utility or REIT would. Flat since the fill (+0.55%). Added 0.5; the residual here is driven by shipyard throughput and milestone execution, uncorrelated with everything else in the book.

Kept as the inflation-hedge counterweight alongside NEM but added only modestly, from 3.5 to 4.0, because the energy setup is genuinely two-sided right now. WTI near $89 and Brent near $100 support international and offshore service capex, and persistently elevated fuel costs were cited by DG as a real squeeze on consumers, confirming the inflation is in the system. Against that, European governments are weighing a release of ~50m barrels of diesel with a possible further ~50m barrels of crude from IEA members, which is an explicit policy cap on near-term prices and is why this is a 4% weight and not an 8% one. At ~1.00 beta it is the highest-beta leg, so restraint here also keeps the required SPY short smaller.

Cut from 5.0 to 3.0 because the thesis is impaired by the company's own disclosure, not by the tape. Management flagged low-income 'spending exhaustion' and rural shoppers limiting trips on elevated fuel, which directly contradicts the trade-down-beneficiary premise this leg was bought on, and the 10-02 payrolls print makes low-income stress worse rather than better. The stock is -22.6% over three months. I am not taking it to zero because at ~16x the $7.10-7.35 FY26 EPS guide with a Moderate Buy consensus and a ~$132.62 mean target, a great deal of the deterioration is already in the price and the residual has reversion potential. But its next print is not until December, so it carries impairment with no catalyst inside this window -- hence a small weight and a tight 14% stop to exit fast if the de-rating continues.

Cut hard from 6.0 to 2.5 on a dated adverse catalyst that lands inside this holding period. A late-September Northeast nor'easter hit Travelers more than any other listed property and casualty carrier because its commercial and personal lines are concentrated in the mid-Atlantic and Northeast, and Q3 results are due 10-16 with elevated catastrophe losses likely. The stock is +1.09% since my 09-30 fill, so the market has not discounted it. The second reason to shrink this leg is that its original thesis was explicitly rate-up: float reinvestment income benefits from a hiking Fed, and October hike odds just fell from 64% to 16%. Two independent premises weakened at once. I keep a 2.5% stub because the 10-year is still 5.28%, hard-market pricing persists, and first-half industry insured losses ran 28% below the ten-year average, so the balance sheet going into the event was strong. 12% stop is the tightest in the book precisely because the downside catalyst has a date on it.

The hedge leg, sized to neutralize index beta rather than to express a market view: the ten longs carry 36.3 points of beta-weighted exposure against a 55% gross long basket for an estimated basket beta of 0.66, so a 36.5% short leaves net index beta at roughly -0.2% of NAV. Trimmed from 38.0 because cutting LVS (~1.05 beta) and TRV and trimming DG lowered basket beta, and an unadjusted hedge would have left the book net short into a tape making new highs on dovish repricing. I deliberately keep the cap-weighted SPY rather than switching to equal-weight RSP: with the top ten names at roughly 40% of index capitalization, a cap-weight-versus-equal-weight divergence at a 50-year extreme, and the Cboe implied-correlation index resuming its decline, shorting the concentrated index against a diversified non-mega-cap basket is part of this book's intended edge. No stop-loss on this leg by design -- a stop on the hedge would un-hedge the book precisely in the rally that makes the hedge necessary, converting a dispersion book into a directional one without my consent.
